availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Debug your current Claude Code session by reading the session debug log. (bundled)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Parallel exploration of docs, code, config, tests, and specs to identify cruft, then interactive triage with clear action options. (project)

availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.name: compact
availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

availableCommands.name: context
availableCommands.description: Show current context usage

availableCommands.name: init
availableCommands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

availableCommands.name: pr-comments
availableCommands.description: Get comments from a GitHub pull request

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Review a pull request

availableCommands.name: security-review
availableCommands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

   421→/**

   424→export type MetaItem = Agent | Workflow | Convention | Observation | Skill;

   426→/**
   427→ * Type guard for skill items
   428→ * Uses _type discriminant field for reliable discrimination
   429→ */
   430→export function isSkill(item: MetaItem | unknown): item is Skill {
   431→  return (
   432→    typeof item === "object" &&
   433→    item !== null &&
   434→    "_type" in item &&
   435→    (item as { _type: unknown })._type === "skill"
   436→  );
   437→}
   438→
   439→/**
   440→ * Determine the type of a meta item
   441→ * AC: @skill-meta-type ac-7 - skills discriminated by _type field
   442→ */
   443→export function getMetaItemType(
   444→  item: MetaItem,
   445→): "agent" | "workflow" | "convention" | "observation" | "skill" {
   446→  if (isSkill(item)) return "skill";
   447→  if ("capabilities" in item) return "agent";
   448→  if ("trigger" in item) return "workflow";
   449→  if ("domain" in item) return "convention";
   450→  return "observation";
   451→}

title: Web UI System
type: module
status:
  maturity: draft
  implementation: implemented
description: >
  Web-based interface for viewing, editing, and managing kspec state. Includes three deployment
  modes:

  1. Local daemon mode - Elysia.js server on Bun with WebSocket for real-time updates

  2. Web dashboard - SvelteKit + shadcn-svelte for full CRUD operations

  3. GitHub Pages export - Static JSON snapshot with read-only SPA for public sharing


  Tech stack: Elysia.js, Bun runtime, WebSocket (not SSE), SvelteKit, shadcn-svelte.

  Distribution via bun build --compile for portable executables.

  - _ulid: 01KFHMFGD2563NGHJWPPXGN9CB
    slugs:
      - daemon-server
    title: Daemon Server Mode
    type: feature
    tags:
      - server
      - websocket
      - elysia
    description: >
      Long-running Elysia.js server on Bun runtime that exposes kspec state via HTTP API and
      WebSocket

      for real-time updates. Binds to localhost only for security. Supports foreground and
      background

      modes with PID file management. Includes heartbeat ping/pong for connection health monitoring.
    depends_on: []
    implements: []
    relates_to: []
    tests: []
    traits:
      - "@trait-json-output"
      - "@trait-error-guidance"
      - "@trait-shadow-commit"
      - "@trait-localhost-security"
      - "@trait-websocket-protocol"
    notes: []
    created: 2026-01-22T01:18:09.314Z
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: ac-1
        given: kspec is installed
        when: user runs 'kspec serve'
        then: Elysia HTTP server starts on configurable port (default 3456) binding to localhost only
      - id: ac-2
        given: daemon is starting
        when: server binds to network interface
        then: only accepts connections from 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (IPv6 localhost)
      - id: ac-3
        given: connection attempt from non-localhost IP
        when: request received
        then: connection rejected with 403 Forbidden
      - id: ac-4
        given: daemon is running
        when: any .kspec/*.yaml file changes
        then: connected WebSocket clients receive update event via topic subscription
      - id: ac-5
        given: file watching is active
        when: rapid changes occur (< 500ms apart)
        then: events are debounced and aggregated into single notification
      - id: ac-6
        given: watched file has YAML parse error
        when: change detected
        then: error logged and WebSocket broadcasts error event (daemon does not crash)
      - id: ac-7
        given: .kspec directory becomes inaccessible
        when: watcher encounters error
        then: daemon logs error and attempts recovery with exponential backoff
      - id: ac-8
        given: Bun fs.watch fails or misses events
        when: reliability issue detected
        then: automatically fall back to Chokidar file watcher
      - id: ac-9
        given: daemon is running
        when: user runs 'kspec serve --daemon'
        then: process detaches to background, writes PID to .kspec/.daemon.pid, CLI returns immediately
      - id: ac-10
        given: daemon is running in background
        when: user runs 'kspec serve stop'
        then: daemon shuts down gracefully, removes PID file, closes all WebSocket connections
      - id: ac-11
        given: daemon is running
        when: GET /api/health is called
        then: returns {status, uptime, connections, version} JSON
      - id: ac-12
        given: daemon receives SIGTERM or SIGINT
        when: shutdown signal received
        then: graceful shutdown (flush pending messages, close connections, save state)
      - id: ac-13
        given: WebSocket connection established
        when: 30 seconds pass without activity
        then: server sends ping frame
      - id: ac-14
        given: ping was sent
        when: no pong received within 90 seconds
        then: connection closed with code 1001
      - id: ac-15
        given: Elysia server is configured
        when: routes are registered
        then: use plugin pattern for middleware (CORS, logging, validation)
      - id: ac-16
        given: daemon code is ready
        when: bun build --compile runs
        then: produces standalone executable without requiring Bun installation
      - id: ac-17
        given: daemon is running with web UI built
        when: browser opens http://localhost:<port>/
        then: serves the built web UI assets (SvelteKit static build) as the root route

    slugs:

    title: Multi-Directory Daemon Architecture
    type: feature
    tags:
      - daemon
      - architecture
      - multi-project
    description: |
      Extends the daemon server to support multiple kspec projects simultaneously from a single
      daemon process. Projects are identified via X-Kspec-Dir HTTP header. Enables E2E testing
      with isolated fixtures and multi-project development workflows.

      Key architectural changes:
      - Global daemon with PID/port files at ~/.config/kspec/
      - Project context caching with on-demand registration
      - Per-project file watchers
      - WebSocket connections bound to specific projects

      BREAKING CHANGE: PID/port files move from .kspec/.daemon.pid to ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid
    depends_on:
      - "@daemon-server"
      - "@api-contract"
    implements: []
    relates_to:
      - "@cli-serve-commands"
    tests: []
    traits:
      - "@trait-localhost-security"
      - "@trait-websocket-protocol"
    notes:
      - _ulid: 01KFQ84FVZB2CWH7Y4GPQR8M9N
        created_at: 2026-01-24T06:00:00.000Z
        author: "@claude"
        content: |
          Design decisions:
          - X-Kspec-Dir header for project selection (clean URLs, easy for clients)
          - Single bundled web UI (consistent version across projects)
          - On-demand project registration (auto-register on first request)
          - No memory limit on cached projects (keep until restart)
          - Global PID at ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid
          - Per-project file watchers
          - Backwards compatible (no header = startup cwd project if valid)
    created: 2026-01-24T06:00:00.000Z
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: ac-1
        given: daemon is running
        when: request includes X-Kspec-Dir header with valid absolute path
        then: daemon uses that project's context for the request
      - id: ac-2
        given: daemon started from directory with .kspec/
        when: request has no X-Kspec-Dir header
        then: daemon uses startup directory's project as default
      - id: ac-3
        given: daemon started from directory without .kspec/
        when: request without X-Kspec-Dir arrives
        then: return 400 with error "No default project configured. Specify X-Kspec-Dir header."
      - id: ac-4
        given: request specifies unknown project path
        when: path is valid kspec project
        then: daemon auto-registers and caches project context
      - id: ac-5
        given: request specifies invalid path (no .kspec/)
        when: request processed
        then: return 400 with error "Invalid kspec project - .kspec/ not found at <path>"
      - id: ac-6
        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
        when: path is relative
        then: reject with 400 and error "Path must be absolute"
      - id: ac-7
        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
        when: path contains ".." segments
        then: reject with 400 and error "Path must not contain parent traversal"
      - id: ac-8
        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
        when: normalized path differs from provided path
        then: use normalized path for registration (resolve "." segments, remove trailing slashes, do NOT
          resolve symlinks)
      - id: ac-8b
        given: X-Kspec-Dir points to path with insufficient read permissions
        when: request processed
        then: return 403 with error "Permission denied - cannot read <path>"
      - id: ac-9
        given: no daemon running
        when: kspec serve start runs from any directory
        then: daemon starts and writes PID to ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid and port to
          ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port
      - id: ac-9b
        given: ~/.config/kspec/ does not exist
        when: daemon starts
        then: create directory with mode 0755 before writing PID/port files
      - id: ac-9c
        given: ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port exists but contains invalid content
        when: CLI reads port
        then: return error "Invalid daemon port file" and suggest "kspec serve stop && kspec serve start"
      - id: ac-10
        given: daemon running on port 3456
        when: kspec serve start runs from different directory
        then: command exits with success and outputs "Daemon already running on port 3456" (no second
          instance started)
      - id: ac-10b
        given: two kspec serve start commands run concurrently (neither has written PID yet)
        when: both check for running daemon
        then: only one daemon starts (use file lock on PID file)
      - id: ac-11
        given: daemon running
        when: kspec serve stop runs from any directory
        then: daemon stops and removes global PID and port files
      - id: ac-12
        given: daemon running
        when: kspec serve status runs
        then: shows daemon status with port, uptime, and list of registered projects with their paths
      - id: ac-13
        given: CLI needs to connect to daemon
        when: daemon is running
        then: CLI reads port from ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port
      - id: ac-14
        given: daemon restarts
        when: first request for a project arrives
        then: project is re-registered automatically (same as initial registration)
      - id: ac-15
        given: daemon running with registered projects
        when: daemon restarts
        then: registered project list is empty (no persistence across restarts)
      - id: ac-16
        given: two concurrent requests for unregistered project with same path
        when: processed
        then: both succeed and share the same registered project context (no duplicate watchers)
      - id: ac-17
        given: project is registered
        when: files change in project's .kspec/
        then: file watcher triggers events scoped to that project
      - id: ac-18
        given: multiple projects registered
        when: Project A changes
        then: only Project A's WebSocket subscribers receive updates
      - id: ac-19
        given: project watcher creation fails due to OS limits (ulimit)
        when: error occurs
        then: project registration fails with 503 and error "Unable to watch project - resource limit
          reached"
      - id: ac-20
        given: registered project's .kspec/ directory is deleted
        when: next request arrives for that project
        then: return 404 and unregister project automatically
      - id: ac-21
        given: WebSocket client connects with X-Kspec-Dir header during handshake
        when: connection established
        then: connection is bound to that project for its lifetime and only receives events from that
          project
      - id: ac-21b
        given: WebSocket connection is established and bound to project
        when: client attempts to change project
        then: project binding is immutable - client must disconnect and reconnect with new header
      - id: ac-22
        given: WebSocket client connects without X-Kspec-Dir header
        when: default project exists
        then: connection is bound to default project
      - id: ac-23
        given: WebSocket client connects without X-Kspec-Dir header
        when: no default project
        then: connection is rejected with close code 4000 and reason "No project specified"
      - id: ac-24
        given: multi-project mode
        when: any API endpoint is called
        then: response data is scoped to the request's project (no cross-project data leakage)
      - id: ac-25
        given: web UI loads
        when: more than one project registered
        then: project selector is shown listing all registered projects
      - id: ac-26
        given: user selects project in UI

        then: all subsequent API requests include that project's path in X-Kspec-Dir header

        given: UI is showing project data

      - id: ac-28
        given: GET /api/projects

        then: returns list of registered projects with paths, registration time, and watcher status
      - id: ac-29
        given: POST /api/projects
        when: called with {path string} body
        then: manually registers a project (for explicit registration use cases)
      - id: ac-30
        given: DELETE /api/projects/:encodedPath
        when: called

        given: X-Kspec-Dir header contains symlinked path

      - id: ac-20b
        given: daemon started from directory with .kspec/ which is later deleted

      - id: ac-11b
        given: daemon is shutting down
        when: shutdown signal received
        then: all project watchers are stopped and all WebSocket connections are closed before process exits

   808→    description: |
   809→      Extends the daemon server to support multiple kspec projects simultaneously from a single
   810→      daemon process. Projects are identified via X-Kspec-Dir HTTP header. Enables E2E testing
   811→      with isolated fixtures and multi-project development workflows.
   812→
   813→      Key architectural changes:
   814→      - Global daemon with PID/port files at ~/.config/kspec/
   815→      - Project context caching with on-demand registration
   816→      - Per-project file watchers
   817→      - WebSocket connections bound to specific projects
   818→
   819→      BREAKING CHANGE: PID/port files move from .kspec/.daemon.pid to ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid

   833→        author: "@claude"
   834→        content: |
   835→          Design decisions:
   836→          - X-Kspec-Dir header for project selection (clean URLs, easy for clients)
   837→          - Single bundled web UI (consistent version across projects)
   838→          - On-demand project registration (auto-register on first request)
   839→          - No memory limit on cached projects (keep until restart)
   840→          - Global PID at ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid
   841→          - Per-project file watchers
   842→          - Backwards compatible (no header = startup cwd project if valid)
   843→    created: 2026-01-24T06:00:00.000Z
   844→    acceptance_criteria:
   845→      - id: ac-1
   846→        given: daemon is running
   847→        when: request includes X-Kspec-Dir header with valid absolute path
   848→        then: daemon uses that project's context for the request
   849→      - id: ac-2
   850→        given: daemon started from directory with .kspec/
   851→        when: request has no X-Kspec-Dir header
   852→        then: daemon uses startup directory's project as default
   853→      - id: ac-3
   854→        given: daemon started from directory without .kspec/
   855→        when: request without X-Kspec-Dir arrives
   856→        then: return 400 with error "No default project configured. Specify X-Kspec-Dir header."
   857→      - id: ac-4
   858→        given: request specifies unknown project path
   859→        when: path is valid kspec project
   860→        then: daemon auto-registers and caches project context
   861→      - id: ac-5
   862→        given: request specifies invalid path (no .kspec/)
   863→        when: request processed
   864→        then: return 400 with error "Invalid kspec project - .kspec/ not found at <path>"
   865→      - id: ac-6
   866→        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
   867→        when: path is relative
   868→        then: reject with 400 and error "Path must be absolute"
   869→      - id: ac-7
   870→        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
   871→        when: path contains ".." segments
   872→        then: reject with 400 and error "Path must not contain parent traversal"
   873→      - id: ac-8
   874→        given: X-Kspec-Dir header value
   875→        when: normalized path differs from provided path
   876→        then: use normalized path for registration (resolve "." segments, remove trailing slashes, do NOT
   877→          resolve symlinks)
   878→      - id: ac-8b
   879→        given: X-Kspec-Dir points to path with insufficient read permissions
   880→        when: request processed
   881→        then: return 403 with error "Permission denied - cannot read <path>"
   882→      - id: ac-9
   883→        given: no daemon running
   884→        when: kspec serve start runs from any directory
   885→        then: daemon starts and writes PID to ~/.config/kspec/daemon.pid and port to
   886→          ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port
   887→      - id: ac-9b
   888→        given: ~/.config/kspec/ does not exist
   889→        when: daemon starts
   890→        then: create directory with mode 0755 before writing PID/port files
   891→      - id: ac-9c
   892→        given: ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port exists but contains invalid content
   893→        when: CLI reads port
   894→        then: return error "Invalid daemon port file" and suggest "kspec serve stop && kspec serve start"
   895→      - id: ac-10
   896→        given: daemon running on port 3456
   897→        when: kspec serve start runs from different directory
   898→        then: command exits with success and outputs "Daemon already running on port 3456" (no second
   899→          instance started)
   900→      - id: ac-10b
   901→        given: two kspec serve start commands run concurrently (neither has written PID yet)
   902→        when: both check for running daemon
   903→        then: only one daemon starts (use file lock on PID file)
   904→      - id: ac-11
   905→        given: daemon running
   906→        when: kspec serve stop runs from any directory
   907→        then: daemon stops and removes global PID and port files
   908→      - id: ac-12
   909→        given: daemon running
   910→        when: kspec serve status runs
   911→        then: shows daemon status with port, uptime, and list of registered projects with their paths
   912→      - id: ac-13
   913→        given: CLI needs to connect to daemon
   914→        when: daemon is running
   915→        then: CLI reads port from ~/.config/kspec/daemon.port
   916→      - id: ac-14
   917→        given: daemon restarts
   918→        when: first request for a project arrives
   919→        then: project is re-registered automatically (same as initial registration)
   920→      - id: ac-15
   921→        given: daemon running with registered projects
   922→        when: daemon restarts
   923→        then: registered project list is empty (no persistence across restarts)
   924→      - id: ac-16
   925→        given: two concurrent requests for unregistered project with same path
   926→        when: processed
   927→        then: both succeed and share the same registered project context (no duplicate watchers)
   928→      - id: ac-17
   929→        given: project is registered
   930→        when: files change in project's .kspec/
   931→        then: file watcher triggers events scoped to that project
   932→      - id: ac-18
   933→        given: multiple projects registered
   934→        when: Project A changes
   935→        then: only Project A's WebSocket subscribers receive updates
   936→      - id: ac-19
   937→        given: project watcher creation fails due to OS limits (ulimit)
   938→        when: error occurs
   939→        then: project registration fails with 503 and error "Unable to watch project - resource limit
   940→          reached"
   941→      - id: ac-20
   942→        given: registered project's .kspec/ directory is deleted
   943→        when: next request arrives for that project
   944→        then: return 404 and unregister project automatically
   945→      - id: ac-21
   946→        given: WebSocket client connects with X-Kspec-Dir header during handshake
   947→        when: connection established
   948→        then: connection is bound to that project for its lifetime and only receives events from that
   949→          project
   950→      - id: ac-21b
   951→        given: WebSocket connection is established and bound to project
   952→        when: client attempts to change project
   953→        then: project binding is immutable - client must disconnect and reconnect with new header
   954→      - id: ac-22
   955→        given: WebSocket client connects without X-Kspec-Dir header

   958→      - id: ac-23
   959→        given: WebSocket client connects without X-Kspec-Dir header
   960→        when: no default project
   961→        then: connection is rejected with close code 4000 and reason "No project specified"
   962→      - id: ac-24
   963→        given: multi-project mode
   964→        when: any API endpoint is called
   965→        then: response data is scoped to the request's project (no cross-project data leakage)
   966→      - id: ac-25

   970→      - id: ac-26
   971→        given: user selects project in UI
   972→        when: selection changes

   974→      - id: ac-27
   975→        given: UI is showing project data
   976→        when: different project selected

   978→      - id: ac-28
   979→        given: GET /api/projects
   980→        when: called
   981→        then: returns list of registered projects with paths, registration time, and watcher status
   982→      - id: ac-29
   983→        given: POST /api/projects
   984→        when: called with {path string} body
   985→        then: manually registers a project (for explicit registration use cases)
   986→      - id: ac-30
   987→        given: DELETE /api/projects/:encodedPath
   988→        when: called

   990→      - id: ac-8c
   991→        given: X-Kspec-Dir header contains symlinked path
   992→        when: path resolves to same directory as another registered project via symlink
   993→        then: paths are treated as separate projects (symlinks are NOT resolved during normalization)
   994→      - id: ac-20b
   995→        given: daemon started from directory with .kspec/ which is later deleted
   996→        when: request without X-Kspec-Dir arrives after default project .kspec/ deleted
   997→        then: return 400 with error 'Default project no longer valid. Specify X-Kspec-Dir header.'

I now have a thorough understanding of the entire codebase. Let me compile the complete picture:

---

## Complete Codebase Exploration Report

### 1. Plan Document (`ui-revamp-plan.md`)

The file `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/.kspec/artifacts/ui-revamp-plan.md` does **not exist**. The `.kspec/artifacts/` directory does not exist. The spec/plan lives inside the YAML module file instead.

---

### 2. Web UI Source Structure

**`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/`**

```
app.css                          # Tailwind v4 + design system tokens
app.d.ts, app.html
lib/
  api.ts                         # HTTP client (daemon + static modes)
  api-static.ts                  # Static snapshot reader
  constants.ts                   # DAEMON_PORT=3456, API_BASE, WS_BASE
  utils.ts
  assets/favicon.svg
  ds/
    tokens.css                   # --design-* CSS custom properties (16 colors, 4 radii, 7 spacing, 7 z-index, 3 fonts, 7 status colors)
    animations.css               # ds-shimmer, ds-breathe keyframes + utility classes
  components/
    Sidebar.svelte               # Grouped nav (Work/Specs/Capture/Config), badge counts
    ConnectionStatus.svelte      # WebSocket status badge
    CommandPalette.svelte, MobileNav.svelte
    TaskList.svelte, TaskFilters.svelte, TaskDetail.svelte, TaskDetailPanel.svelte
    ItemTree.svelte, ItemDetail.svelte
    ProjectSelector.svelte, ReadOnlyBanner.svelte
    ui/                          # shadcn-svelte: accordion, badge, button, card, command, data-table, dialog, input, select, separator, sheet, sidebar, skeleton, table, tabs, textarea, tooltip
  stores/
    connection.svelte.ts         # WebSocket state (connectionState, connectionLost)
    mode.svelte.ts               # 'loading' | 'daemon' | 'static' AppMode
    project.svelte.ts            # Project selection + X-Kspec-Dir header
    taskDetail.svelte.ts
  types/
    snapshot.ts                  # Re-exports from @kynetic-ai/shared
    triage.ts
  hooks/is-mobile.svelte.ts
  websocket/
    manager.ts                   # WebSocketManager class (backoff, dedup, re-subscribe)
    types.ts                     # ConnectionState, Subscription, etc.
routes/
  +layout.svelte                 # SidebarProvider, initMode, loadProjects, initConnection
  +page.svelte                   # Dashboard: task counts by status
  agents/+page.svelte            # STUB: "Agent definitions and dispatch status will appear here."
  sessions/+page.svelte          # STUB: "Session history will appear here."
  tasks/+page.svelte             # Full implementation with filters, list, slide-over detail panel
  items/+page.svelte, inbox/+page.svelte, observations/+page.svelte
  plans/+page.svelte, specs/+page.svelte, triage/+page.svelte
  validate/+page.svelte, workflows/+page.svelte, settings/+page.svelte
```

---

### 3. Existing Route Patterns (from `/tasks/+page.svelte`)

Key patterns used throughout:

- **Svelte 5 runes**: `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, `$props`
- **Data loading**: `onMount` + `$effect` watching `getProjectVersion()` for project-change reloads
- **WebSocket**: `subscribe(['tasks'])`, `on('tasks', handler)` in `onMount`; `off`/`unsubscribe` in `onDestroy`
- **Loading/error states**: `loading = $state(true)`, `error = $state('')`
- **Static mode**: `isStaticMode()` guard, `assertWritable()` before mutations
- **Navigation**: `$page.url.searchParams` for URL-driven filtering
- **AC annotation**: `// AC: @spec-ref ac-N` comments on relevant code sections

---

### 4. Design System (`lib/ds/`)

**tokens.css** defines `--design-*` CSS custom properties, mapped via `app.css`'s `@theme inline` block to Tailwind utility classes:

| Token Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Colors (16) | `bg-design-bg`, `text-design-fg`, `bg-design-card`, `bg-design-primary` |
| Status Colors (7) | `bg-status-pending` (amber), `bg-status-in-progress` (orange), `bg-status-pending-review` (blue), `bg-status-needs-work` (yellow), `bg-status-completed` (emerald), `bg-status-blocked` (red), `bg-status-cancelled` (gray) |
| Radii | `rounded-design-sm/md/lg/xl` |
| Spacing | `p-design-xs/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/3xl` |
| Z-index | `z-design-base/dropdown/sticky/overlay/modal/popover/toast` |
| Fonts | `font-design-sans`, `font-mono` |

**animations.css** defines:
- `.ds-shimmer` — skeleton loading (gated behind `prefers-reduced-motion`)
- `.ds-breathe` — active agent pulse indicator (box-shadow pulse, 3s ease-in-out)

---

### 5. API Types (`packages/shared/src/api.ts`)

Key interfaces relevant to agents/sessions:

```typescript
// Agent definition (legacy spec type)
interface Agent {
  _ulid: string; slugs: string[]; role: string; status: string;
  capabilities: string[]; constraints: string[];
}

// What GET /api/agent/status actually returns (NOT the shared Agent type):
// {
//   dispatch_enabled: boolean,
//   active_invocations: Array<{ session_id, agent_id, task_ref, elapsed_ms }>,
//   queue_depth: number,
//   agent_definitions: Array<{ id, name, adapter }>
// }
```

---

### 6. Daemon API Endpoints Relevant to Agents/Sessions

**`packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts`** provides:

| Endpoint | Method | Returns |
|---|---|---|
